'''Geoffrey Walsh Davies'''<ref name=":0" /> (15 December 1938 – 13 July 2023) was an English [[actor]]. He is best known for his role as Dr. Dick Stuart-Clark in all seven of the [[Doctor in the House (franchise)|''Doctors'']] programmes that aired from 1969 to 1991. 

== Early life ==
Geoffrey Walsh Davies was born in Leeds to Harry and Emma Davies.<ref name=":0" /> His father was an accountant.<ref name=":0" /> Davies was educated at grammar school and studied at art college to be a [[commercial art]]ist at the card and board games manufacturer Waddingtons<ref name=":0" />

Geoffrey left Waddingtons after he was called up for national service.<ref name=":0" /> After he left national service, he decided to become an actor and worked with a drama group at the Leeds Civic Theatre in the evenings.<ref name=":0" /> After being suggested by a journalist, Geoffrey joined the White Rose Players repertory company in [[Harrogate]] as a stage director, also working in Sheffield, before doing a two-year course at the [[Royal Academy of Dramatic Art]] at the suggestion of [[Benjamin Whitrow]].<ref name=":0" /> 

== Career ==
While he was still at RADA, he was spotted by a member of [[Noël Coward]]'s company, who got him his first role in the film ''[[Oh! What a Lovely War]]'' as Lieutenant Faversham.<ref name=":0" />

A year after he left drama school, he was cast as Dr. Dick Stuart-Clark in the sitcom [[Doctor in the House (TV series)|''Doctor in the House'']].<ref name=":0" /> Davies later revealed that he didn't get the role at first: "I spoke to my agent when I heard that ITV were casting Doctor in the House, but every part had gone, then, the actor who was due to play medical student Dr Stuart-Clark dropped out and I got an audition".<ref name=":0" /> He is the only member of the original cast to have performed in all the sequels, ''[[Doctor at Large (TV series)|Doctor at Large]]'', ''[[Doctor in Charge]]'', ''[[Doctor at Sea (TV series)|Doctor at Sea]]'', ''[[Doctor on the Go]]'', ''[[Doctor Down Under]]'' – filmed in Australia – and ''[[Doctor at the Top]]''. Davies was "so convincing" as an actor that one time he was actually mistaken as a person in the medical field: "I once pulled up at a traffic accident to see if everything was all right when someone saw me and said, 'It’s OK, we’ve got a doctor'".<ref name=":0" /> Davies also appeared in the shows stage production that toured in [[Australia]] in 1974, and its follow up show ''Doctor in Love'' in 1979.<ref name=":0" />

Davies moved with the cast of Doctor Down Under to [[Australia]] from 1979 to 1980, and for four episodes from 1981 to 1984, Davies went to [[Jersey]] to play Roger Dubree in the crime drama show [[Bergerac (TV series)|Bergerac]].<ref name=":0" /> Back in the UK, he appeared in ''[[Bergerac (TV series)|Bergerac]]'' and at [[Windsor, Berkshire|Windsor]] and [[the Old Vic]] where he was in ''[[The Ghost Train (play)|The Ghost Train]]''. Davies also appeared in a [[Cinderella]] pantomime, where he played the role of [[Buttons (pantomime)|Buttons]], the servant of Cinderella's stepfather, and Cinderella's friend. He toured a number of times in the [[Far East]] as well as Australia and New Zealand. Davies said of working in theatre: "Television is fun, but there’s nothing like going out on stage and playing to a live audience".<ref name=":0" />

In 1992 he played a barrister in an episode of [[Families (TV series)|''Families'']], which also featured his daughter [[Emma Davies (actress)|Emma]] and in 2002, he played Judge Phelps-Gordon, who sentenced [[Little Mo Mitchell]] to prison for murder, in five episodes of ''[[EastEnders]]''.<ref name=":0" /> Also in 2002, he was in the stage show Murdered to Death, a spoof on [[Agatha Christie]]'s novels.<ref name=":0" /> His last roles were in 2012; one as a clown in an episode of the Television show ''[[Not Going Out]]'' and as a man in a queue in the film [[Run for Your Wife (2012 film)|''Run for Your Wife'']].<ref name=":0" />

==Personal life and death==
Davies was married to Ann Wheeler Davies since 1962.<ref name=":0" /> Their daughter, [[Emma Davies (actress)|Emma Davies]], is also an actress having appeared in film and television roles since the mid-1980s. He has a grandchild.<ref name=":0" />

Geoffrey Davies died on 13 July 2023, at the age of 84.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last1=Hayward |first1=Anthony |title=Geoffrey Davies obituary |url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2023/sep/17/geoffrey-davies-obituary |access-date=17 September 2023 |work=The Guardian |date=17 September 2023}}</ref>
